decision: Not adopted: an exception to 'commit the floor churn make test leaves' for a dependency floor that bmk lowered or moved back across a major version.
reopen_if: A bmk run lowers a dependency floor again, or bmk's CHANGELOG reverts the 3.22.7 behaviour.
why: Fixed in bmk itself: since 3.22.7 bmk no longer lowers a dependency floor when no single release installs on every supported Python, so the churn the skill says to commit no longer holds a lowered floor.

decision: Not adopted: advice that bmk's floor update can pick a release PyPI is still uploading, so a red gate should be re-run after restoring pyproject.toml and uv.lock.
reopen_if: bmk drops or shortens its cooldown, or a gate fails resolving a third-party release younger than the cooldown.
why: Measured on bmk 3.33.1: bmk writes its 7-day cooldown into the project before locking and judges a third-party floor only against releases uploaded before that cutoff, so a release minutes old cannot be chosen. Index lag on the project's own freshly published package is already covered in the skill.

decision: Not adopted: having bmk pin every declared floor younger than the cooldown, existing floors included, before its first lock attempt.
reopen_if: A bmk deps update leaves a declared floor younger than the cooldown unpinned, with that run's full update_deps output kept.
why: Did not reproduce on bmk 3.33.2: replaying the reported pyproject.toml against PyPI as of the reported cutoff wrote the young floor's exclude-newer pin along with the others, and a real bmk deps update on a copy pinned and passed. Other projects with the same young floor got the same pin at the time. The failing run's log was gone; the likeliest cause is a transient PyPI answer whose one-line notice a filtered view of the output hid.
